summary: Pocahontas County, WV CCC-built 40-ft steel lookout (1940), last staffed 1965; tower gone, with concrete remains described on a Red Spruce Knob trail.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; a trail guide describes concrete remains on Red Spruce Knob, which we take to be this site (not stated outright by any source)

access.note: Trail guide describes a 2.5-mile out-and-back hike to the site from the Highland Scenic Highway; no closure noted in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Hike of 2.5 miles out and back, starting right off the Highland Scenic Highway, about 20 minutes from downtown Marlinton; only remains are described, not a tower

events.note: Built with CCC labor; 40-foot steel tower with a 14x14 cab
Lookout William McCloud logged a storm of severe winds and lightning on April 19, 1963, as quoted in the forest history
Last year the tower was staffed
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: built 1940 by CCC labor; 40-foot steel tower with 14x14 cab; last staffed 1965
evidence.quote: This 40' steel tower was built in 1940 by CCC labor. It featured a 14'x14' cab. It was last staffed in 1965.

evidence.supports: erected 1940 using Civilian Conservation Corps labor; 40-foot steel tower with 14 x 14 foot cab
evidence.quote: 1940: A 40-foot steel tower with a 14' x 14' cab was erected using Civilian Conservation Corps labor.

evidence.supports: 1965 was the last year the lookout was staffed
evidence.quote: 1965: The last year that the lookout was staffed.

evidence.supports: location Monongahela National Forest, Pocahontas County, West Virginia
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
listed in the West Virginia site list as Tower Gone
evidence.quote: Red Spruce Pocahontas 38.32655 -80.15409 Tower Gone FFLOS US 167, WV 17

evidence.supports: Red Spruce Tower (1940) was among the nine towers the CCC built on the Monongahela between 1933 and 1945
evidence.quote: Gaudineer Knob Tower (1936); Red Spruce Tower (1940); and Mikes Knob Tower (1941).

evidence.supports: CCC built the greatest period of towers on the forest between 1933 and 1945
evidence.quote: However, the greatest period of fire tower construction on the Monongahela occurred between 1933 and 1945 with the addition of 13 fire towers.

evidence.supports: lookout William McCloud on duty at the Red Spruce tower during the April 19, 1963 storm, with three hours of severe winds
evidence.quote: William McCloud, Red Spruce Tower Lookout, endured three hours of severe winds and
relentless lightning as an electrical storm battered his home in the sky

evidence.supports: most Monongahela towers were razed, leaving concrete piers and steps
evidence.quote: simply razed, leaving only their concrete piers and steps as the evidence of their existence.

evidence.supports: a 2.5-mile out-and-back hike off the Highland Scenic Highway, about 20 minutes from Marlinton; the guide places a fire tower site on Red Spruce Knob
evidence.quote: Red Spruce Knob is a 2.5-mile out-and-back hike right off the Highland Scenic Highway, just 20 minutes from downtown Marlinton.

evidence.supports: concrete remains of the tower can be seen in the center of the loop, with old metal equipment
evidence.quote: The concrete remains of the tower can be seen in the center of the loop, along with some old metal equipment.

evidence.supports: a stone foundation piece remains at the Red Spruce Knob fire tower site
evidence.quote: Remaining stone foundation piece of the Red Spruce Knob Fire Tower site.

sources.title: Fire Towers: Fifty Years of Early Detection and Fire Protection
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Monongahela National Forest

notes_for_editor: The link between the Red Spruce Knob trail guide's fire tower site and the register's Red Spruce Tower Site is inferred from the matching names only; the register coordinates were not checked against the knob. Not used: a Facebook post in search results saying 'Red Spruce Knob ... Removed in 1968' (social post, unverified, possibly a different site). The exact year the tower came down is not in any source read. The guide has photos of the remains that were not downloaded.
